Attendance and participation at the City of La Verne Development Review Committee meetings are
welcomed and appreciated. Community engagement provides the Development Review Committee
with valuable information. Regular Meetings are held on the 1st Tuesday of every month. In
compliance with the American Disabilities Act, any person with a disability who requires a modification
or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the City Clerk’s Office at (909)
596-8726 at least 48 hours prior to the meeting.

The Council Chambers will be open to the public at 9:00 a.m. Materials related to an item on this
agenda, submitted to the Development Review Committee after distribution of the agenda packet, are
available for public inspection at the meeting or in the Community Development Department during
normal business hours.

FROM:  Candice Bowcock, Planning Manager
SUBJECT:  GILEAD SCIENCES – L50 COLD STORAGE EXPANSION AND PARKING
  DETERMINATION

SUMMARY
Gilead Sciences, Inc. is requesting a Precise Plan Review approval for an approximately
12,748-square-foot expansion of the existing L50 Warehouse/Packaging building at 1800
Wheeler Avenue to provide new temperature-controlled pharmaceutical storage and related
support areas. The project will remove 34 parking spaces and add four replacement spaces,
resulting in 628 total parking spaces on the campus. The applicant is also requesting a parking
determination based on the operational characteristics of the facility. The property is located
within the Arrow Corridor Specific Plan and is governed by the Gilead Development Agreement,
originally approved in 2016 and extended in 2026 through May 5, 2031. The extension did not
modify the approved land uses, development standards, or development intensity.

RECOMMENDATION
The Development Review Committee is recommended to:

1. Determine that the proposed L50 Cold Storage Expansion remains within the scope of the
previously adopted Initial Study/Mitigated Negative Declaration and subsequent Addendum and
that no further environmental review is required pursuant to CEQA Guidelines Section 15162;

2. Approve Case No. 89-26PPR for an approximately 12,748-square-foot expansion of the
existing L50 Warehouse/Packaging building to accommodate cold-storage and related support
facilities, subject to the applicable conditions of approval and final review by City departments;
and

3. Approve the parking determination for the Gilead campus pursuant to La Verne Municipal
Code Sections 18.76.040 and 18.76.160, determining that the unoccupied cold-storage,
equipment and associated support areas, and the campus circulation/utility spine do not
generate independent parking demand, resulting in a minimum parking requirement of 606
spaces, with 628 spaces provided following construction of the project.

DISCUSSION

Background and Development Agreement
The Gilead campus was originally approved as a pharmaceutical manufacturing campus
through a variety of land-use entitlements, including Precise Plan Review Case No. 56-14PPR,
associated subdivision and variance approvals, and Development Agreement Case No. 79-

  Page 6 of 27
   Gilead Sciences – L50 Cold Storage Expansion and Parking Determination, Page 2

14DA. The Development Agreement establishes the development framework for the campus
and requires Phase II development to obtain Precise Plan Review approval from the
Development Review Committee. In 2026, the City approved a First Amendment extending the
Development Agreement through May 5, 2031. The amendment addressed applicable impact
fees but did not increase development intensity, change permitted uses, or modify the
development standards or project entitlements established by the original Agreement.
The proposed L50 expansion continues the existing pharmaceutical manufacturing, storage and
distribution functions of the campus and does not introduce a new land use. Following
construction, the campus would contain approximately 352,994 square feet of entitlement area.
Staff therefore finds the project consistent with the Development Agreement and applicable
campus entitlements.

Proposed Building Expansion
The project consists of an approximately 12,748-square-foot expansion of the existing L50
Warehouse/Packaging building for specialized pharmaceutical cold storage. The addition will
include -40°C freezer storage, 2°C to 8°C refrigerated storage, staging and warehouse areas,
equipment and support spaces, and associated mechanical systems. Most of the addition will
be occupied by refrigerated storage systems, equipment, racks, and required access areas. No
additional employees or separate work shifts are proposed. Existing L50 employees will access
the storage areas as needed for material movement. The addition is proposed to use smooth-
face concrete masonry units painted to match the existing L50 building, including existing
accent-band treatments. The proposed parapet will match the existing building and will not
exceed 55 feet.

The property is located within the Business Park area of the Arrow Corridor Specific Plan. The
proposed L50 expansion complies with the applicable development standards for the site. The
addition is located within the existing Gilead campus and does not encroach into the required
setbacks. Building coverage will remain below the applicable maximum lot coverage of 50
percent. The proposed building height will not exceed 55 feet, consistent with the previously
approved height variance for the Gilead campus and the existing approvals incorporated into
the Development Agreement. Accordingly, the proposed addition is consistent with the
applicable setback, lot coverage, and height requirements governing the site.

Parking
Gilead's campus includes a mix of manufacturing, warehouse, and office functions. Therefore,
the City's original approval applied the parking ratio associated with each use: one space per
500 square feet for industrial/manufacturing, one per 1,000 square feet for warehouse/storage,
and one per 250 square feet for office uses. Section 18.76.040(B) of the La Verne Municipal
Code authorizes the Development Review Committee to determine parking requirements for
uses not specifically listed in the parking table, while Section 18.76.160 provides for
interpretation when the appropriate classification is unclear. Staff has evaluated the proposed
expansion based on the operational characteristics of the facility below.

Cold-Storage Area: Of the approximately 12,748-square-foot addition, approximately 1,660
square feet will function as occupied staging/warehouse space and will continue to be parked at
the warehouse ratio of one space per 1,000 square feet. The remaining approximately 11,088
square feet consists of cold-storage chambers, equipment and related unoccupied support and
access areas. These areas will not contain permanently assigned employees or independently

  Page 7 of 27
   Gilead Sciences – L50 Cold Storage Expansion and Parking Determination, Page 3

generate employee, visitor or customer parking demand. Staff therefore recommends that the
DRC exclude this area from the parking calculation. Any future conversion to regularly occupied
space would require reevaluation of the parking requirement.

Campus Spine: The campus includes an approximately 18,830-square-foot circulation and
utility spine (Spine) connecting the buildings. Although historically included in the warehouse
parking calculation, the Spine functions solely as internal circulation for employees and
materials and does not generate parking demand. Staff therefore recommends excluding the
Spine from the parking calculation, reducing the campus parking requirement by approximately
19 spaces.

Parking Supply and Observed Demand
The campus currently contains 658 parking spaces. The project will remove 34 spaces and
construct four replacement spaces, resulting in 628 total spaces after construction. Parking
surveys conducted during 14 periods in July and August 2026 identified a maximum observed
occupancy of 483 vehicles, leaving at least 175 vacant onsite spaces during the survey period.
With the recommended parking classifications, the campus would require 606 spaces and
provide 628, resulting in a 22-space surplus. Staff finds the proposed parking spaces are
adequate to serve the campus.

Proposed Parking Calculations:

Site Design, Circulation, and Landscaping
The addition will be constructed along an existing service-oriented portion of the L50 building.
Existing parking and landscaping within the building footprint will be removed, including four
trees, which will be replaced as part of the proposed landscaping improvements. The project
also includes new hardscape, four replacement parking spaces and modifications to the existing
fire-access area. Final plans shall comply with applicable parking, landscaping, accessibility,
circulation, and Fire Department requirements.

Fire Department Review
The La Verne Fire Department reviewed the proposed expansion and issued comments dated
September 8, 2026. The building exceeds 30 feet in height, therefore aerial apparatus access is
required. Final fire lanes, apparatus access, grades, landscaping, and other potential
obstructions shall comply with the 2025 California Fire Code and be approved by the Fire
Department. The addition will connect to the existing onsite fire-protection water supply and fire
pump system. Hydraulic calculations will be required to demonstrate adequate fire flow and

  Page 8 of 27
   Gilead Sciences – L50 Cold Storage Expansion and Parking Determination, Page 4

system capacity. The building will also require an NFPA 13 automatic sprinkler system, with fire
alarm and sprinkler plans submitted separately for Fire Department review. The proposed high-
piled storage rack system and stored commodities will require separate submittals addressing
rack configuration, storage height, aisle widths, commodity classifications, and applicable fire-
protection requirements. The conceptual plans depict a potential new Fire Department
Connection. However, the need for and final location of a new FDC will be determined during
formal plan check based on the final sprinkler and hydraulic design. Roof access may be
required depending on the final building configuration. The project will also be required to
comply with applicable Knox access, construction fire-safety and all-weather access
requirements. Final approval remains subject to formal Fire Department plan check and
compliance with all applicable fire and life-safety standards.

Precise Plan Review Findings
Section 18.16.100 of the La Verne Municipal Code requires the Development Review
Committee to consider consistency with applicable planning documents, site design, circulation,
parking and loading, architecture, landscaping, building height, environmental impacts, and
compatibility with surrounding development. Staff finds that the proposed L50 expansion
satisfies these requirements. The project is consistent with the existing pharmaceutical campus
use, the Arrow Corridor Specific Plan, the Development Agreement, and applicable existing
approvals. The proposed site design maintains adequate circulation and parking, the building
addition is designed to complement the existing L50 facility, and landscaping displaced by
construction will be replaced. Final plans will remain subject to applicable conditions of approval
and review by Fire, Engineering, Building, and other City departments.

COMPATIBILITY WITH SURROUNDING USES
The proposed project is located entirely within the existing Gilead Sciences campus and
represents an expansion of an existing building. The proposed cold-storage use is directly
related to Gilead's existing pharmaceutical operations and does not introduce a new or
incompatible land use. The addition is located within an existing industrial/business-park and
will be constructed using materials and colors intended to coordinate with the existing L50
building. The proposed smooth-faced CMU exterior will be painted to match the existing
building and will incorporate similar accent bands, allowing the addition to read as part of the
existing campus rather than as an unrelated structure. The project is not anticipated to increase
traffic or parking demand because the applicant has indicated that no additional employees or
separate shifts will be created as a result of the cold-storage expansion. Mechanical and
refrigeration equipment associated with the cold-storage system shall be designed, screened
and operated in compliance with applicable City noise and development standards. Final plans
will also be reviewed for lighting, landscaping, fire access, drainage, and utility compliance.
Based on the continued use, location of the addition, architectural treatment, and no increase in
employment or visitor activity, staff finds that the proposed project will remain compatible with
surrounding uses and with the character of the Gilead campus and surrounding Business Park
area.

ENVIRONMENTAL ANALYSIS
The Gilead campus and associated development approvals were previously evaluated under
CEQA through an Initial Study/Mitigated Negative Declaration and subsequent Addendum. The
proposed L50 Cold Storage Expansion remains within the previously approved campus
development framework and does not introduce a new land use or increase development

  Page 9 of 27
   Gilead Sciences – L50 Cold Storage Expansion and Parking Determination, Page 5

intensity beyond that previously contemplated. The approximately 12,748-square-foot
expansion will primarily provide temperature-controlled storage and related equipment space,
with no additional employees or dedicated work shift proposed. Site-specific requirements
related to construction, mechanical equipment, hazardous materials, fire access, drainage,
landscaping, and lighting will remain subject to applicable mitigation measures, regulations and
City plan review. Staff has not identified substantial project changes, changed circumstances, or
new information that would result in new or substantially more severe environmental impacts.
Therefore, pursuant to CEQA Guidelines Section 15162, no subsequent environmental
document is required, and the Development Review Committee may rely on the previously
adopted Initial Study/Mitigated Negative Declaration and Addendum for the proposed Precise
Plan Review.

Dear Mr. Rosenberg:

On October 6, 2026, the City of La Verne Development Review Committee considered
Case No. 89-26PPR, a request for Precise Plan Review approval of an approximately
12,748-square-foot expansion of the existing L50 Warehouse/Packaging building at 1800
Wheeler Avenue. The expansion will accommodate temperature-controlled pharmaceutical
storage, staging, equipment and related support areas, together with associated parking,
landscaping, utility and fire-access improvements.

The Development Review Committee hereby conditionally approves Case No. 89-26PPR,
subject to the findings and conditions below.

Pursuant to La Verne Municipal Code Sections 18.76.040(B) and 18.76.160, the
Development Review Committee reviewed the parking requirements applicable to the
Gilead pharmaceutical campus.

The DRC determines that:

  1. Approximately 1,660 square feet of occupied staging/warehouse area within the
  expansion shall be parked at the warehouse ratio of one space per 1,000 square
  feet.
  2. Approximately 11,088 square feet of cold-storage, equipment and unoccupied
  support areas does not independently generate parking demand and is excluded
  from the parking calculation.
  3. Approximately 18,830 square feet of campus circulation and utility Spine area does
  not independently generate parking demand and is excluded from the parking
  calculation.

Based on these determinations, the campus requires 606 parking spaces. Following
construction, 628 spaces will remain, providing a surplus of 22 spaces. Any future
conversion of the excluded areas to regularly occupied or employee-generating uses shall

In accordance with chapter 18.16 of the La Verne Municipal Code, your project has been
conditionally approved based upon the following findings:

1. The subject application is consistent with the general plan and conforms to all
  specific plans, zoning, and other applicable ordinances and subdivision
  requirements and resolutions.

  The subject property is located within the Business Park area of the Arrow Corridor
  Specific Plan and is developed as the existing Gilead pharmaceutical manufacturing
  campus. The proposed cold-storage expansion supports the existing pharmaceutical
  manufacturing, warehousing, and distribution functions and does not introduce a new
  land use. The property is also governed by the Development Agreement originally
  approved under Case No. 79-14DA. The Development Agreement, as amended in 2026,
  remains in effect through May 5, 2031 and provides for subsequent campus
  development through Precise Plan Review. The First Amendment did not increase
  development intensity or alter permitted land uses or development standards. The
  proposed project remains within the development framework established by the existing
  approvals and Development Agreement.

2. The site is safe, functional and environmentally sensitive to the  surroundings.
  Grading, where required, minimizes environmental  damage  to the extent
  possible.

  The proposed addition is located adjacent to the existing L50 Warehouse/Packaging
  building within the developed Gilead campus. The project maintains the campus's
  existing circulation pattern and provides adequate vehicle, pedestrian, loading and
  emergency access subject to final departmental review. The project will remove 34
  parking spaces and construct four replacement spaces, resulting in 628 parking spaces
  following construction. Based upon the parking determination approved with this Precise
  Plan Review, 606 spaces are required, providing a surplus of 22 spaces. Parking counts
  submitted by the applicant also documented at least 175 vacant onsite spaces during the
  survey periods. Fire apparatus access, fire flow, landscaping, drainage, accessibility and
  utility improvements will be reviewed through the applicable Fire Department, Public
  Works, Engineering and Building plan-check processes.

3. The architecture proposed observes community standards and protects the
  character of the adjacent development.

  The addition is designed as an extension of the existing L50 building. Proposed smooth-
  face concrete masonry units will be painted to match the existing building, including its
  accent-band treatment. The proposed building height is consistent with the height
  established for the existing campus development. The addition is located within an

  existing industrial/pharmaceutical campus and will not substantially alter the visual
  character of development along Wheeler Avenue or the surrounding Business Park area.

4. The landscaping plan ensures visual relief, providing an attractive environment
  for the public’s enjoyment.

  Construction of the addition requires removal of existing landscape improvements and
  four existing trees within the project area. The proposed plans provide replacement
  landscaping and four replacement trees adjacent to the building expansion and
  replacement parking area. Final landscape and irrigation plans will be required to comply
  with applicable City landscape and water-efficiency standards and Fire Department

Approval of Case No. 89-26PPR is subject to the following conditions:

General

  1. The applicant shall comply with the City's Standard List of Conditions, which is
  incorporated into this approval.

  2. The project shall be developed in substantial conformance with the approved plans

  3. Exterior materials, colors and architectural treatments shall substantially conform to

  Department approval.

  4. Any revision to the approved building footprint, use, height, architecture, parking,
  circulation or landscaping shall be reviewed by the Community Development
  Department to determine whether additional approval is required.

  5. The project shall remain consistent with Development Agreement Case No. 79-14DA,
  as amended, and all applicable existing approvals.

Parking and Circulation

  6. A minimum of 606 parking spaces shall be maintained onsite unless otherwise
  approved pursuant to the La Verne Municipal Code.

  7. The approximately 11,088 square feet of cold-storage, equipment and unoccupied
  support space is excluded from required parking only while those areas remain
  unoccupied and do not independently generate parking demand.
